hypothesis: Predict the ordering of two span treatment effects inside the same training history, at the same first/last stage and fixed other action. Remove history-level skill preferences before transferring this ordering. The background is a training match only; a future action is never required to score the current span. Adapt the regularized least-squares preference-difference objective of Pahikkala et al. (https://staff.cs.utu.fi/~aatapa/publications/jPaTsAiJaBo09a.full.pdf).
features: Use only the current chronological source's original Qwen 96-word anonymized single-turn and paired-group chunks. Represent a turn by the unit-normalized mean of its unit single-chunk vectors. Compute the best own vs best unrelated chunk cosine under each grouping. Four coordinates per turn: paired-minus-single own score, paired-minus-single own-minus-distractor margin, cosine to its actual adjacent grouping partner, and that cosine minus the best nonpartner turn cosine. Unavailable distractor or partner contributes cosine zero. The session features are the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles of each coordinate. No target question, absolute date, native outcome, memory created by a pending action, or other target session is used.
matched_fit: Original panel: collapse the 452 question contrasts into all 60 physical comparisons. Raw and verified credit targets are separate question-means, including zeros. Within each stage compare every two distinct sources with the same donor history and other action bit. One donor history has unit total pair weight. Hold the entire target history out before making pairs, rotating credit labels, standardizing features, finding centers, fitting coefficients or calibrating amplitudes. Standardize by equally weighted donor histories and their unique nodes with coordinate SD floor .02. Fit pair-difference ridge with dimensionless penalty .5. Center each inferred score at the equal-history mean training node and divide by max(.01, interquartile range of the donor-node scores); clip shifts to +/-2 log odds above the same repaired raw-return actor. The primary uses only verified credit corrections. Controls use raw rank targets, equally matched cyclic permutations of credit within each donor's same-stage/background group, the same credit score at fixed .05 scale, raw+credit joint scores, native, terminal, raw-return and the original passage actor. Compare with pivot-rate matching.
expanded_fit: Predeclared after the first of five earlier terminal audits was confirmed, before outcomes of the other four were used. Separately add all 12 earlier terminal source sessions from the six histories to credit training only. Sum newly confirmed signed credit on that decision and divide by the full number of registered questions in its original window. Other questions contribute zero extra feedback. Retain failures/vetoes in this denominator. Match by actual preceding action. Use the same 60-comparison raw fold for both variants. Include original actor probabilities as a control. Earlier root cases remain outside this terminal expansion. Bind original and new label, source and trace hashes.
audit_and_gates: Predict each held donor edge's relative raw treatment effect and relative verified credit before inspecting that history's outcomes. Report predicted/actual ties separately, direction concordance, errors vs constant zero and history-level results. Compare focal, four-path replica, 99 full-prefix endpoints, per-question costs, action draws, paired and HT F1, fixed-direction ceilings and strict-prospective counts. Use the standard complete 40-window/378-question later and 99-endpoint/185-question prefix gate, +.02 over native/terminal, positive HT vs both, improvements over raw-return, raw ranking, rotated labels and matched use, four matched-rate winning histories, and positive strict and exact-replica over native/raw. Expanded must also beat the earlier ranker. Keep both independent datasets locked until development promotion.
